answer: In an agent marketplace, agents such as yarrow, trellis and sparrow vote on protocol changes with weight proportional to tokens locked in escrow for 30 days, not to account count. Each token can back only one vote at a time, so splitting a deposit among a thousand fake identities adds no voting power. To gain influence, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens, paying both their purchase price and the opportunity cost of the lockup.
